description: Looking for ambitious and passionate science lovers.
summary: ASTROCARE is an interactive web-based health monitoring prototype designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It helps astronauts perform daily health check-ins, monitor important physical and mental health indicators, identify unusual changes, and receive preventive health guidance. The platform includes a health dashboard, self-assessment form, health insights, illustrative trend visualization, body-system education, and preventive reminders. ASTROCARE aims to improve astronaut health awareness and support timely communication with mission medical teams
details:
ASTROCARE: Astronaut Self-Health Monitoring & Early Warning System

What it does. On a long space mission, help from Earth-based doctors can be slow or limited. ASTROCARE gives astronauts a simple daily check-in. They enter their heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, sleep, mood and stress level. The app then shows a plain summary, marks anything that looks unusual, and suggests a sensible next step, such as resting, rechecking, or contacting the mission medical team. It also has a simple trend chart, short guides on how spaceflight affects the heart, bones, immune system, sleep, mind and radiation exposure, and daily reminders for exercise, sleep, water and food.

Benefits and impact. The goal is to help astronauts notice small changes early and look after their mental health as well as their physical health. We hope it encourages regular check-ins, helps crew members compare themselves with their own normal, and makes conversations with flight doctors clearer and quicker.

Tools used. HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with SVG for the charts. It is a responsive web page, and all analysis runs in the browser, so no data leaves the device.

What is creative about it. Most health tools focus only on numbers. ASTROCARE puts body readings, mood, learning and prevention together in one calm, easy screen that is quick to use even when an astronaut is tired. It is also designed to adapt to spacecraft, lunar habitats and Mars habitats.

Things we considered. We kept the interface simple for people working under pressure. The alert rules are only illustrative, not medical limits, and the app does not diagnose anything. We also thought about privacy by keeping everything on the device. In future versions we would add secure storage, wearable sensors, personal baselines and alert limits approved by mission doctors.
